questions.q: How does monitoring differ from the one-time rule checks taught in Chapter 4?
options: Monitoring runs the check on a schedule, stores a history, compares results to an expected range, and alerts automatically instead of requiring someone to run it by hand
Monitoring uses a completely different query language than rule checks
Monitoring only applies to pipeline jobs, never to data values
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: A rule check answers whether data is bad right now; monitoring answers that continuously, without anyone needing to ask.

questions.q: Why is "pipeline health" worth monitoring separately from data quality rule results?
options: A data quality rule can't catch bad data from a load that never ran at all
Pipeline health and data quality are the same metric
Pipeline health only matters for real-time streaming systems
It's a legal requirement in most industries
questions.explain: If a job silently fails to run, every rule check against that table could show misleadingly clean (stale) results.

questions.q: What is "drift" in the context of data quality monitoring?
options: A metric that is slowly getting worse over time without yet crossing a hard threshold
A sudden, one-time spike in a data quality metric
The process of moving data between two different warehouses
A synonym for a referential integrity violation
questions.explain: A null rate creeping from 1% to 6% over months might never breach a hard threshold but is still worth surfacing.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what characterizes a good alert?
options: It fires on an agreed threshold rather than noise, routes to an actual owner, explains what broke, and distinguishes severity levels
It fires on every single fluctuation to be maximally thorough
It is always sent to a shared inbox so everyone sees it
It never needs to specify what table or report is affected
questions.explain: Over-alerting causes alert fatigue — alerts get ignored once there are too many non-actionable ones.

questions.q: How does monitoring connect to the next two lessons in this chapter?
options: The pass-rate history monitoring builds feeds scorecards, and unresolved alerts become candidates for tracked issues
Monitoring replaces the need for scorecards and issue tracking entirely
Monitoring only connects to Chapter 4's rules, not to later lessons
Scorecards and issue tracking happen before monitoring in the workflow
questions.explain: Monitoring's output is the raw material Lesson 27's scorecards visualize and Lesson 28's issue log tracks.
